sections.h2: What makes Sumter County different from other Florida counties?
sections.html:
Sumter County has the oldest population of the four counties in this set by a wide margin: the Census Bureau reports 57.6 percent of residents are 65 or older and only 7.6 percent are under 18. The mid-2025 estimate of 157,772 residents is 21.6 percent above the 2020 base of 129,752.

Households average just 1.93 people, and owners occupy 87.6 percent of homes. Only 25.8 percent of residents 16 and older are in the civilian labor force. For a seller, that profile means many buyers are retirees who care about carrying costs, homestead rules and what the first tax bill looks like after they move in.

sections.h2: How big is Sumter County and how fast is it building?
sections.html:
Sumter covers 557.13 square miles of land. Density rose from 170.8 people per square mile in 2010 to 232.9 in 2020. Housing units reached 95,691 in the July 2025 estimate, and the Census counted 3,516 building permits for 2025.

Ongoing construction means a seller may compete with new homes, and new construction also adds to the tax base that the county and school board use when setting millage. Median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 was $385,400, with median monthly owner costs of $1,686 for owners with a mortgage and $602 without one.

sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Sumter County?
sections.html:
The Sumter County Property Appraiser sets values and handles homestead, widow, widower and veteran exemptions, and the tax collector bills and collects. The clerk of the circuit court also serves as the clerk to the Value Adjustment Board.

The county's own page says that board is independent of the property appraiser and consists of two county commissioners, one school board member and two citizen members, one appointed by the commission and one by the school board. It hears appeals of values, classifications and exemptions, has no control over tax rates, and cannot reduce a value or grant an exemption because of personal hardship. Special magistrates, who are qualified appraisers or attorneys, hold the hearings and make recommendations.

sections.h2: What dates drive the Sumter County tax year?
sections.html:
The statewide calendar applies. Property is assessed as of January 1, homestead and classification applications are due March 1, and tangible personal property returns are due April 1.

The Notice of Proposed Property Taxes comes in August, and a challenge to value is filed with the clerk within 25 days. Denied exemptions, classifications or portability have their own 30-day window after the denial letter is mailed. Bills arrive in November, discounted 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent from November through February, and taxes unpaid after April 1 are delinquent.

  • March 1: exemption filing.
  • August: TRIM notice.
  • 25 days later: value petition closes.
  • November: bills and 4 percent discount.
  • April 1: delinquency.

sections.h2: How do homestead and portability work for Sumter County sellers?
sections.html:
Florida's homestead exemption is up to $50,000, with $25,000 applying to school taxes and a second amount to other taxes above $50,000 of value. The owner must have made the home a permanent residence by January 1, and the application goes to the property appraiser on Form DR-501.

On a sale, the next January 1 reassessment lifts the property to market value, so a buyer's first full bill can be much higher than the seller's. A seller moving within Florida can port up to $500,000 of the capped difference to the next homestead, provided that home is established within three years, with Form DR-501T filed alongside the application. A seller leaving the state loses the benefit, since portability only applies between Florida homes.

sections.h2: Which exemptions matter most in a county this old?
sections.html:
Age-based and veteran benefits are likely to come up in many Sumter County sales. The state lets counties and cities adopt an additional homestead exemption of up to $50,000 for owners 65 or older within an income limit, and a further exemption equal to the assessed value for long-term residents with a just value under $250,000, subject to income.

  • Veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability: homestead discount equal to the VA percentage.
  • Disabled former servicemembers rated 10 percent or more: $5,000 off assessed value.
  • Total and permanent service-connected disability: possible total exemption on homestead.

Ask the Sumter County Property Appraiser whether local ordinances add to the state list, and whether a surviving spouse keeps a benefit after a death.

sections.h2: What does a Sumter County deed cost at closing?
sections.html:
The state charges seventy cents on each $100 of the price, and the clerk takes it at recording. A mortgage the buyer assumes counts toward the price.

Each party on the deed is liable, so the contract should state who funds it. Clerk charges begin at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for later pages, plus add-ons. Estate sales get one relief: a deed from a personal representative under a probated will is listed as not taxable, though a plain family deed for estate planning has no exemption.

sections.h2: What happens to a Sumter County house with unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Taxes left unpaid lead to certificates sold by June 1, and the holder may seek a deed after two years. The clerk runs the tax deed auction, where the winning bidder leaves a deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is more, and pays the rest within 24 hours not counting weekends and holidays.

A seller sidesteps all of that by paying at closing. Ask the collector for a payoff, and ask your title agent for a certificate search, before signing a contract.

faqs.q: How many Sumter County residents are 65 or older?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists 57.6 percent of Sumter County residents as 65 or older, the highest share among the four counties in this set.

faqs.q: When is the Sumter County homestead deadline?
faqs.a: March 1 of the tax year, filed with the Sumter County Property Appraiser on Form DR-501 or the office's online filing.

faqs.q: Who hears assessment appeals in Sumter County?
faqs.a: The Value Adjustment Board, an independent five-member panel, with hearings run by special magistrates. The clerk serves as its clerk.

faqs.q: Does the Value Adjustment Board cut taxes for hardship?
faqs.a: No. The county's page says it cannot change an assessed value or grant an exemption or classification based on personal hardship.

faqs.q: Is there a deed tax when selling in Sumter County?
faqs.a: Yes, 70 cents per $100 of consideration, paid to the clerk at recording.
